clue.text: Undercover, American seen on rugby pitch twice?

indicators.note: something seen on a pitch stands within its bounds, so one piece sits between the ends of the other

blocks.note: a rugby pitch has an H-shaped set of posts at each end
the whole of the first build is repeated

explanation.surface: An American spectator at a rugby match is mistaken for someone undercover, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: Rugby goalposts are shaped like a letter H, one set at each end of the pitch, so an American seen on the pitch stands between two Hs.
explanation.definitionFit: Hush-hush is an informal adjective for secret, kept quiet, as undercover work is.

clue.text: Ivy can be found in impoverished eras

indicators.note: the answer is said to be found inside the following words, spanning their letters

blocks.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Ivy grows over ruins in poor times.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedera is the botanical genus name of ivy, the climbing evergreen plant.

clue.text: They fly nighttime weapon aboard planes

indicators.note: something aboard a vessel is carried inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: to plane wood is to smooth it, as one sands it

explanation.surface: A night raid in which a weapon is carried in aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Planes' looks like aircraft but is the verb: to plane wood smooths it down, as sanding does. The weapon goes in just before the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The sand dart is a European moth, one of the many night-flying insects.

clue.text: Work close up with the Beeb to install lake observatory

indicators.note: to work material is to knead and reshape it, so these letters are reshaped
installing something fixes it inside, so one letter is put in among the others

explanation.surface: A BBC crew films close up at a lakeside observatory.
explanation.walkthrough: The Beeb is a nickname for the BBC, the British broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hubble Space Telescope is an orbiting astronomical instrument, an observatory in space.

clue.text: Group of undergrads mostly smearing bananas

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of the word is dropped
bananas is slang for crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Students in a hall of residence messing about with fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminar is a small university class where a tutor and students discuss a subject.

clue.text: Protection for art students in the first instance sitting practice exams

indicators.note: the first instance of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: British schools sit mock exams before the real ones

explanation.surface: What art students wear when they first sit their trial exams.
explanation.walkthrough: Mocks are practice exams taken in British schools before the real GCSEs or A levels.
explanation.definitionFit: Smocks are loose overgarments worn to keep paint off clothes, typical of art students.

clue.text: What may make you lament?

blocks.note: surface reading: a cause of grief or sorrow
setter's reading: the six letters of the word lament can be rearranged from an adjective meaning of the mind

explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically, the letters of MENTAL broken down make LAMENT, so a MENTAL BREAKDOWN is what makes 'lament'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mental breakdown is a period of acute psychological distress, which would certainly give cause to lament.

clue.text: Ludwig in bed, a heavenly body?!

indicators.note: one thing in another goes inside it

blocks.note: the setter refers to himself, so his name stands for ME

explanation.surface: The setter, tucked up in bed, asks whether he is a heavenly body.
explanation.walkthrough: When a setter names himself in his own clue, the name stands for the first person.
explanation.definitionFit: A comet is an icy celestial object orbiting the sun, one of the bodies in the heavens.

clue.text: Safest for armistices, on reflection, to include El Salvador

indicators.note: a reflection shows things back to front, so the word is read the other way
including something takes it inside, so a piece goes into the other

blocks.note: truces are agreements to stop fighting
the international vehicle code for El Salvador

explanation.surface: Peace deals involving El Salvador judged the safest option.
explanation.walkthrough: International vehicle registration codes are a common crossword source for country abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Securest is the superlative of secure, meaning most protected from danger, so a synonym of safest.

clue.text: I announce small potato

definitions.note: the answer speaks of itself: a stater is one who says 'I announce'

explanation.surface: Someone proudly declaring that they are a small potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small potato' looks like one phrase meaning an unimportant person; it splits into S and TATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A stater is a person who states things, and stating is announcing, so a stater could say this of himself.

clue.text: Star knocked back nearly a half of Benedictine

indicators.note: nearly means falling just short, so the last letter of that portion is dropped
something knocked back is pushed the other way, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: roughly the first half of the liqueur's eleven-letter name

explanation.surface: Someone knocks back most of a glass of liqueur and feels a star.
explanation.walkthrough: Benedictine is a herbal liqueur, and 'knocked back' suggests drinking; here it reverses BENED.
explanation.definitionFit: Deneb is the brightest star in the constellation Cygnus, the swan.

clue.text: Regrettably icy moment, representative of the bigger picture

indicators.note: something done regrettably has gone wrong, so the letters come out wrongly ordered

explanation.surface: A frosty moment captured in a snapshot that sums up a wider situation.
explanation.definitionFit: Metonymy is the figure of speech where a part or associated thing stands for the whole, as 'the crown' for royalty.

clue.text: Stopped by Port of London Authority, bill recalled for our neighbour

indicators.note: something recalled is called back, so its letters are read backwards
a flow stopped by a plug has the plug lodged inside it

blocks.note: a tender is an offer of payment; legal tender is money

explanation.surface: A port authority blocks an invoice that was withdrawn from a neighbour.
explanation.walkthrough: TENDER reversed is REDNET, and the Port of London Authority's PLA is put in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Mars, called the Red Planet for its rusty colour, is Earth's planetary neighbour.

clue.text: Reportedly change train's destination?

indicators.note: reportedly means as heard spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: to change something is to modify it

explanation.surface: A rail announcement that a train's terminus has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: The train is a bride's long trailing dress, not a railway one; it heads up the aisle.
explanation.definitionFit: A bride's train follows her down the aisle to the altar in church, where the wedding happens.

clue.text: Provide food including – finally! – sugar bowl

indicators.note: including something takes it inside, so a letter goes into the word
finally points to the very end of the word, its closing letter

explanation.surface: A caterer serving sugar in a bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped hollow in the ground, as made by a meteor or volcano.

clue.text: Picture puzzles – about 16 and more?

blocks.note: the answer to 16, a school bus, and others like it

explanation.surface: Puzzles about a school bus and more.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 refers to the answer SCHOOL BUS; plural vehicles of that kind are BUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures and symbols represent words or syllables.

clue.text: What may be booked for field trip? Inappropriately, Soho clubs

definitions.text: What may be booked for field trip?

indicators.note: done inappropriately means set out wrongly, so the letters are out of place

explanation.surface: A school outing that inappropriately ends up in Soho nightclubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Soho is London's nightlife district, an unlikely field trip destination.
explanation.definitionFit: A school bus is hired to carry pupils on outings, so one is reserved for an excursion.

clue.text: Loosened rivets on wall of toilet facility, being playful

indicators.note: loosened parts come apart and move, so the letters shift around
forming the wall of something means surrounding it, so these letters go around the other piece

blocks.note: a po is a chamber pot

explanation.surface: A workman loosens bolts on the wall of a public lavatory.
explanation.walkthrough: A po is an old British word for a chamber pot; the rearranged letters form a wall around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportive is a literary adjective meaning frolicsome or inclined to play.

clue.text: Almost hassle-free, they're used with mortars

indicators.note: almost means not quite complete, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: as a suffix, -free means without, as -less does

explanation.surface: A claim that something is nearly hassle-free, about kitchen tools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' as in sugar-free is the suffix -less, as in sugarless.
explanation.definitionFit: A pestle is the club-shaped tool used to grind substances in a mortar bowl.

clue.text: Spelling bee?

blocks.note: surface reading: a competition where children spell words aloud
setter's reading: casting spells, and a bee is a gathering, so a gathering of witches

explanation.walkthrough: A bee is a social gathering for a purpose, as in a quilting bee; spelling is casting spells.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabbat is a midnight assembly of witches, a meeting of those who cast spells.

clue.text: Appropriate drinks passed around local characters

indicators.note: something passed around another encircles it, so one piece is placed outside the other

blocks.note: beers, fitting drinks for a pub
a local is a pub, and PH is the map abbreviation for public house

explanation.surface: Fitting drinks handed round in a pub to the regulars.
explanation.walkthrough: A local is a British pub near home; PH is how maps mark one. 'Characters' looks like the pub's regulars but means letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Aleph is the first letter of the Hebrew alphabet, so alephs are written characters.

clue.text: Made tipsy upon entering wicked world of scholarship

indicators.note: a tipsy person staggers about, so the letters are jumbled
entering something means going inside it

explanation.surface: Someone got drunk on arrival in a sinful world of academics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wicked' looks like evil, but it is slang for great, as ace is.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the community and environment of universities and scholarly learning.

clue.text: Genius running after salamander

indicators.note: one thing coming after another is placed second, so the clue's first piece goes at the end

blocks.note: a newt is a small salamander
a machine that is running is on

explanation.surface: A clever person chasing a salamander.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac Newton, discoverer of gravity's laws, is the archetypal scientific genius.

clue.text: Some are Olympian, running these round their rivals?

definitions.note: completes the idiom 'run rings round', to outclass easily

blocks.note: first meaning: the five interlocking circles of the Olympic flag
second meaning: the idiom for beating opponents with ease

explanation.walkthrough: Two senses combine: the Olympic symbol, and the idiom 'run rings round' meaning to beat easily.
explanation.definitionFit: Rings are circles; the Olympic emblem is five of them, and great athletes figuratively run them round rivals.

clue.text: Stars suddenly brighter and twinkly on average, before storm

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the preceding letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Stars that brighten and twinkle like an average sky before bad weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storm' looks like weather but is the verb: ON and AVE are stormed into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A nova is a star that flares up suddenly to great brightness before fading; novae is the plural.

clue.text: Star has been here – problem for Starmer's lot?

blocks.note: first meaning: the collapsed remnant of a massive star
second meaning: an unexplained shortfall in public finances

explanation.walkthrough: Starmer's lot is Keir Starmer's Labour government, which blamed its predecessors for a gap in the nation's budget.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomically, the collapsed core of a dead star; financially, a gap where money has vanished from the accounts.

clue.text: Uninjured? Surprisingly alive, having got on it

indicators.note: a surprising result comes out in an unexpected form, so the letters appear in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone emerges unhurt and astonishingly still alive after getting on with it.
explanation.definitionFit: Inviolate means untouched and unharmed, kept free from injury or violation.

clue.text: Gold piece: ring

explanation.surface: A golden piece of jewellery: a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbit is a circular path around a body, and circle or ring can mean the same.

clue.text: Old flame damaged tree somewhere in Devon

indicators.note: something damaged is knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A former lover vandalised a tree in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Devon is a county in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Exeter is the county town and cathedral city of Devon.

clue.text: Laureate composed sonnet about New York

indicators.note: something composed is put together anew, so the letters are arranged afresh
about means surrounding, so these letters go around the other piece

explanation.surface: A poet laureate wrote a sonnet about New York.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred, Lord Tennyson was Britain's Poet Laureate for most of Queen Victoria's reign.
